title: They Offered It to Him for Free… But Abraham Refused — And What He Did Instead Will Expose the Way You Value God
paragraphs: They Offered It to Him for Free… But Abraham Refused — And What He Did Instead Will Expose the Way You Value God
There’s a moment in Scripture that most people read too quickly… and because of that, they miss the weight of it.

Genesis 23 is not loud. It’s not dramatic like fire from heaven. It’s quiet… grief-filled… almost uncomfortable. Sarah is gone. The woman who walked through promises, barrenness, laughter, and covenant is now lifeless.
Abraham is broken.
And in the middle of his mourning, something unexpected happens.
He refuses a free gift.
Read it slowly.
“None of you will refuse me your cave for burying my dead,” Abraham says. And the Hittites respond generously. Ephron even offers the field and the cave freely.
But Abraham answers:
“I will give you money for the field; take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.” (Genesis 23:13)
The Hebrew here is piercing.
“נָתֹן אֶתֵּן כֶּסֶף” (naton eten keseph)
Literally: “Giving I will give silver.”
It’s not casual. It’s emphatic. Determined. Almost stubborn.
Abraham insists.
He will not take what costs him nothing.
And if you sit with that long enough… it begins to confront something inside you.
Because we live in a generation that loves free things.
Free grace… without repentance.
Free forgiveness… without surrender.
Free salvation… without transformation.
But Abraham understood something that many modern believers have quietly forgotten.
What is sacred must never be treated as cheap.
David would later echo this same conviction when he said:
“I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God that cost me nothing.” (2 Samuel 24:24)
In Hebrew:

“לֹא־אַעֲלֶה לַיהוָה עֹלוֹת חִנָּם”
(lo a'aleh laYHWH olot chinnam)
“I will not lift up to the LORD offerings for free… for nothing… without cost.”
Do you see the pattern?
Men who truly walked with God refused to give Him what required no sacrifice.
Because deep down… they understood the nature of covenant.
Grace is free to receive… but never cheap to carry.
Abraham wasn’t just buying land.
He was honouring a promise.
God had told him this land would belong to his descendants. But at that moment, Abraham owned nothing… except a grave.
And instead of grabbing something freely… he paid full price.
Four hundred shekels of silver.
Publicly weighed.
Witnessed.
Sealed.
Why?
Because this wasn’t just a transaction.
It was faith made visible.
It was worship expressed through cost.
It was a declaration:
“This matters too much to treat casually.”
And if we’re honest…
Somewhere along the way, we started treating holy things casually.
Prayer became optional.
Obedience became negotiable.
Conviction became uncomfortable… so we avoided it.
We wanted the promise… without the altar.
We wanted resurrection… without death.
But the Gospel has never worked like that.
Jesus didn’t redeem you cheaply.
The Greek says in 1 Peter 1:18–19:

“οὐ φθαρτοῖς… ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι Χριστοῦ”
(ou phthartois… alla timiō haimati Christou)
“Not with perishable things… but with the precious blood of Christ.”
τιμίῳ (timiō) — precious, costly, of great value.
You were not purchased with something disposable.
You were bought with something infinitely costly.
And when that reality truly hits you… it changes how you live.
It changes what you tolerate.
It changes what you compromise.
It changes what you’re willing to sacrifice.
Abraham stood in grief… holding loss in his hands… and still chose honour over convenience.
He chose cost over comfort.
He chose reverence over opportunity.
And that decision still echoes today.
Because every believer eventually faces a moment like this.
A moment where you can take the easy way… or the costly one.
Where you can treat God casually… or honour Him deeply.
Where you can receive without surrender… or give Him everything.
Be honest.
Which one have you been choosing lately?
This isn’t about money.
This is about your heart posture.
Because the truth is… many people want a relationship with God that requires nothing.
No dying to self.
No surrender of pride.
No repentance from hidden sin.
No cost.
But that’s not covenant.
That’s convenience.
And convenience never transforms anyone.
Grace transforms you.
But only when you stop treating it like it’s cheap.
Abraham’s decision wasn’t about a burial plot.
It was about identity.
He wasn’t just a man receiving land.
He was a man walking in promise.
And people who walk in promise don’t cut corners with God.
They honour Him… even when it costs them.
Especially when it costs them.
So let this sit with you for a moment…
What have you been offering God lately?
Is it something that costs you nothing?
Or something that reflects His worth?
Because deep down… you already know the answer.
And maybe this is the moment where everything shifts.
Maybe this is where you stop negotiating with God… and start surrendering to Him.
Maybe this is where the comfortable version of your faith dies… and the real one begins.
Be honest. This hit deeper than you expected.
And don’t keep this to yourself.
And if you feel something stirring in your spirit right now… don’t ignore it.
And if you truly want to glorify God with your life… not just in words but in action… then step into deeper discipleship.
This isn’t about content.
This is about transformation.
This is about becoming the kind of believer who doesn’t offer God what costs nothing.
Because at the end of it all… you won’t be remembered for what you received freely…
…but for what you were willing to surrender.
And that’s where everything changes.
